correctness_confidence.basis: The paper rigorously formalizes 18 constructive theorems in Lean 4 without any sorry, warnings, or Classical.choice, and verifies exact game trees across 16 canonical certificates with 60/60 adversarial test rejections.

novelty.basis: First machine-checked zero-floating-point formalization and exact combinatorial game-tree auditor for normal/misère grid NoGo PSPACE-completeness and Coins-are-Lava subcubic bipartite graph reductions.

reproducibility.basis: Fully specified with complete Lean 4 theorem identifiers, explicit verification modes, latency benchmarks (0.060–6.495 ms), and SHA-256 manifest checks across 41 tracked artifacts.

rigor.basis: Detailed algebraic invariants, rope-width separations (2tw + 1 < Nw), B2CL move budgets, and comprehensive adversarial red-team testing covering 60 distinct attack vectors.

significance.basis: Milestone in formalized combinatorial game theory, providing machine-checked exact-integer certificates for foundational PSPACE-completeness results in placement games.

potential_errors: Scope is explicitly restricted to finite combinatorial, algebraic, truth-table, parity, and minimax cores, leaving full Turing-machine PSPACE reductions and asymptotic planar layout routing for future work.
strengths: 18 zero-dependency constructive theorems in Lean 4 with 0 sorry and 0 Classical.choice.
Pure-stdlib exact-integer game verifier NOGO-PSPACE-CERT-1.0 with zero floating-point operations.
Robust red-team adversarial suite successfully rejecting 60/60 live forgery attacks.
Comprehensive empirical atlas covering grid minimax state counts and subcubic bipartite graph winner flips.
strong_novelty_candidates: Machine-checked zero-floating-point formalization of B2CL gadget move budgets and Coins-are-Lava rope-width separations.
Exact combinatorial game-tree auditor with 16 canonical certificates and 60/60 adversarial rejections.
summary: The manuscript presents a rigorous machine-checked formalization and exact game-tree audit for the PSPACE-completeness results of Burke, Davies, and Tennenhouse on normal/misère grid NoGo and subcubic bipartite Graph NoGo via Coins-are-Lava. Using an 18-theorem zero-dependency Lean 4 kernel and the NOGO-PSPACE-CERT-1.0 pure-stdlib verifier, the work successfully repplays 16 canonical certificates and rejects 60/60 adversarial forgeries.
weaknesses: Discussion of omitted full Turing-machine PSPACE reductions and planar layout routing is brief.
